Definition: from (the alternate of) G4936; a running together, i.e. (riotous) concourse:--run together.
BiblicalUsage: At Jerusalem all the city is moved, and the people run together and take Paul and drag him out of the temple. A running together can be a mob, and this one is: the city moves as one body against one man, and the doors shut behind him.
TheologicalSignificance: What grips me is that a crowd running together is easily a mob, and I hold that I must not join a running crowd until I know what it is running for.
